components.notes: Table rows for all four named fragments: Monadic FOL 199-210, FO2 212-223, GF 225-236, Bernays-Schoenfinkel/EPR 238-248. Named systems unchanged.

Each of the four rows states its language restrictions (unary predicates/no identity or functions 201-203; two variables, relational, equality optional 214-216; guard condition 227-230; prenex exists*forall*, function-free, identity omitted 241-244) and its decision complexity (NEXPTIME/coNEXPTIME 204-208; NEXPTIME 217-220; 2EXPTIME/EXPTIME 231-234; NEXPTIME 245-246), with the complexity classes defined at 167-186.

components.gap: Only one of the four required fragments has an undecidable boundary case stated: FO2 -> three-variable relational fragment undecidable (lines 221-223). The other boundary entries for the required fragments name exclusions without any undecidable boundary case: Monadic FOL (209-210) only says equality/constants/functions are outside the cited complexity claim, and gives no undecidable extension (e.g. adding a single binary predicate); GF (235-236) only says loosely guarded and fixed-point extensions are different rows, with no undecidable extension of the guarded fragment; Bernays-Schoenfinkel/EPR (247-248) only says the reversed prefix, equality and function symbols are not included, with no undecidable prefix class or extension. The remaining undecidability statements are outside the four required fragments: the Presburger row with multiplication (259-262) is an extra row, and lines 271-273 cite only unrestricted first-order validity, not a boundary case of any named fragment; line 273-274 explicitly declines to assert undecidability for excluded features.
